original_question: Does there exist any α > 0 for which the universal weak-coupling slope m_α of the copolymer critical curve equals 1/(1+α)? Here m_α is defined by h_c(λ) ~ m_α λ for small λ when the limit exists, and the question asks whether the lower-bound expression 1/(1+α) is ever the exact value of the slope for the original copolymer model.
target_in_paper: Section 1.4, second open sub-problem after Theorem 1 and bounds (18)-(19): "is m_α = 1/(1+α) for some α > 0?" ([fcaraven.github.io](https://fcaraven.github.io/download/papers/cgt.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's intended open problem very closely: it asks about the universal weak-coupling slope m_α, it targets the lower-bound value 1/(1+α), and it is aimed at the original/discrete copolymer model rather than the reduced model for which equality is known to hold for all α in (0,1). ([fcaraven.github.io](https://fcaraven.github.io/download/papers/cgt.pdf))
missing_details: The paper's ambient object is the general discrete α-copolymer model of Section 1.2, not only the original simple-random-walk copolymer: τ is a persistent renewal with K(n) ~ C_K n^{-(1+α)}, and the disorder ω is IID with E[ω_1]=0, E[ω_1^2]=1, and M(t)=E[e^{tω_1}]<∞ for every t. ([fcaraven.github.io](https://fcaraven.github.io/download/papers/cgt.pdf))

A fully stand-alone version should say that h_c(λ) is the quenched critical curve separating localization and delocalization for this model. ([fcaraven.github.io](https://fcaraven.github.io/download/papers/cgt.pdf))

The phrase "when the limit exists" is weaker than the paper's actual weak-coupling statement in the relevant regime: for α in (0,1), Section 4/Theorem 2 proves that m_α = lim_{λ↓0} h_c(λ)/λ exists and is universal. For α≥1, the paper explicitly warns that existence of m_α is not guaranteed and one should speak of liminf/limsup instead. ([fcaraven.github.io](https://fcaraven.github.io/download/papers/cgt.pdf))

The question is posed against the quantitative context of Theorem 1 and bounds (18)-(19): 1/(1+α) ≤ m_α < 1, with a sharper lower bound known for some α. That context explains why asking for equality with 1/(1+α) is a sharp, nontrivial question. ([fcaraven.github.io](https://fcaraven.github.io/download/papers/cgt.pdf))

If you want to keep the phrase "original copolymer model," the paper-faithful contrast is with the reduced model mentioned immediately afterward, for which m_α = 1/(1+α) for all α in (0,1). ([fcaraven.github.io](https://fcaraven.github.io/download/papers/cgt.pdf))
refined_question: For the discrete α-copolymer model of Section 1.2—namely, a copolymer built from a persistent renewal law K(n) ~ C_K n^{-(1+α)} with α>0 and IID disorder ω satisfying E[ω_1]=0, E[ω_1^2]=1, and E[e^{tω_1}]<∞ for all t—let h_c(λ) denote the quenched critical curve. In the weak-coupling regime α∈(0,1), Theorem 2 shows that the universal slope m_α := lim_{λ↓0} h_c(λ)/λ exists, while Theorem 1 gives the lower bound m_α ≥ 1/(1+α). Does there exist any α∈(0,1) for which this lower bound is actually sharp, i.e. m_α = 1/(1+α), for the original discrete copolymer model? ([fcaraven.github.io](https://fcaraven.github.io/download/papers/cgt.pdf))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in the paper. Section 1.4 first states the bounds on m_α coming from Theorem 1 and then, in the immediately following discussion, lists exactly two open sub-problems, the second being whether m_α can equal 1/(1+α) for some α>0. Section 4 provides the hidden assumptions needed to make that question stand alone: for α∈(0,1), m_α is the universal weak-coupling slope because lim_{λ↓0} h_c(λ)/λ exists and equals the slope of the continuum critical curve. The refined version therefore restores the model class, the definition of h_c, the theorem-backed existence range for m_α, and the contrast with the reduced model. ([fcaraven.github.io](https://fcaraven.github.io/download/papers/cgt.pdf))
